# Playground

Paste your `alertmanager.yml`, or the [Kubernetes Secret, Helm values, Mimir config or
AlertmanagerConfig resources](../kubernetes.md) that hold it, and amlint checks it as you
type. You see the findings and the lines they point at, the route tree, where an alert is
delivered, and how a change affects routing. Add Prometheus alerting rules to check routes
against the alerts that exist.

**Your config stays in your browser.** amlint runs in this page as Python compiled to
WebAssembly. Nothing you paste or type is uploaded, and once the page has loaded it needs no
network.

??? info "How it works, and limits"
    - The page downloads [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) (Python for the browser) from the
      jsDelivr CDN, plus the amlint wheel built from this site's sources. Your browser
      caches them, so later visits start faster. None of the page's requests contains your
      config.
    - Checks run in a Web Worker (a background thread of the page) and call amlint's own
      `--format json` output, so the results match `amlint check`, `amlint route` and
      `amlint diff`.
    - **Share link** puts the config, compressed, into the URL after `#`. Browsers don't
      send that part to any server, including this one. But anyone you give the link to can
      read the config, so remove secrets first; the page lists the lines that may hold them.
    - The page doesn't keep your config anywhere. Reload it and your edits are gone.
    - `template-file-missing` isn't checked for a plain `alertmanager.yml`, because its
      template files aren't in the browser. Run `amlint check` on your machine or in CI for
      that. Template files that ship in a Secret or in Helm values are checked under
      Findings, but not in the Diff tab.


---

Source: https://danikdanik2013.github.io/amlint/github-action/

# GitHub Action

Run amlint on every push and pull request with one workflow step. Findings show up as
annotations on the pull request diff, the job fails on errors, and the action can post a
comment that shows which alerts a change routes differently.

## Quickstart

```yaml
# .github/workflows/alertmanager.yml
name: Lint Alertmanager config

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: danikdanik2013/amlint@v0.6.1
        with:
          config-path: alertmanager.yml
```

Each finding becomes an annotation on the line it points at. The job fails on ERROR
findings; add `strict: true` to fail on WARN findings too.

`config-path` can be a plain `alertmanager.yml` or any file from
[Kubernetes & Mimir](kubernetes.md): a Secret, Helm values, a Mimir config or
`AlertmanagerConfig` resources. amlint detects the format from the content.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `config-path` | required | The file to lint (one file) |
| `strict` | `false` | Fail on WARN as well as ERROR (`--strict`) |
| `ignore` | `""` | Comma-separated check codes to skip (`--ignore`) |
| `only` | `""` | Comma-separated check codes to run, and no others (`--only`) |
| `format` | `github` | `github`: findings become annotations. `text`: the console report in the job log |
| `sarif` | `false` | Also upload findings to GitHub code scanning as SARIF ([below](#with-code-scanning-annotations)) |
| `diff-base` | `""` | Git ref to compare `config-path` against; posts the routing diff as a PR comment ([below](#routing-diff-as-a-pr-comment)) |
| `github-token` | `github.token` | Token used to post the routing diff comment |
| `version` | `""` (latest) | amlint version to install from PyPI, e.g. `0.6.1` ([below](#pinning-a-version)) |

## Post the routing diff on pull requests { #routing-diff-as-a-pr-comment }

Set `diff-base` to the pull request's base commit. The action then compares your config with
its version at that commit, using
[`amlint diff --format markdown`](usage.md#markdown-report), and posts the result as one PR
comment. Each push updates the same comment. When routes changed, the comment includes a
diagram of them.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/alertmanager.yml
name: Lint Alertmanager config

on: [push, pull_request]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write   # to create and update the comment

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0   # the base commit has to be in the checkout
      - uses: danikdanik2013/amlint@v0.6.1
        with:
          config-path: alertmanager.yml
          diff-base: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
```

The comment has a summary line, then the label sets (combinations of alert labels) whose
receivers changed, changed `group_by` and timings, and new and fixed findings with their
`file:line:col`. Sections with nothing in them are left out. For example:

> ### amlint diff
>
> **2 routing changes** · no new findings · 0 fixed · 0 unchanged · 6 label sets checked
>
> #### Receivers
>
> | labels | before | after |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | `team=db, severity=critical` | `pagerduty-db` | `slack-db` |
>
> #### Grouping and timings
>
> | labels | receiver | setting | before | after |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | `team=infra` (+1 similar) | `infra-slack` | `group_wait` | `30s` | `10s` |
>
> <sub>Compared with `alertmanager.yml` at 3f2c1a9d8e7b. Updated on every push.</sub>

`(+1 similar)` means one more label set has exactly the same change.

How it behaves:

- **Pull requests only.** It runs on `pull_request` and `pull_request_target` events. On
  other events, such as a push, the step is skipped.
- **One comment.** The comment starts with a hidden `<!-- amlint-routing-diff -->` marker,
  which is how the action finds it again. It posts with `curl` and the GitHub REST API, with
  no third-party actions.
- **New config.** If the file doesn't exist at the base commit, it is new in the PR. The
  diff runs against an empty config, so every finding is new and every receiver was
  `(none)` before.
- **No change.** If the file is the same as at the base and there is no comment yet,
  nothing is posted. An existing comment is still updated, so it doesn't go stale after a
  revert.
- **Job summary.** The report is also written to the job summary. Look there on pull
  requests from forks: their `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only, so the comment can't be posted,
  and the step logs a warning instead of failing.
- **Never fails on findings.** The routing diff is informational. If `amlint diff` can't
  read a config, the step logs a warning and posts nothing.
- **Needs the base commit.** If the base commit isn't in the checkout, the step fails and
  says how to fix it. `fetch-depth: 0` is the simplest fix. Fetching only the base commit
  works too:

    ```yaml
          - uses: actions/checkout@v7
          - run: git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
    ```

- `ignore` and `only` apply to the findings in the comment too.
- A report longer than GitHub allows in a comment is cut at 65,000 characters. Run
  `amlint diff` locally for the rest.

## Upload to code scanning { #with-code-scanning-annotations }

To also see findings in the repository's **Security** tab, turn on `sarif`. The repository
needs GitHub code scanning (free for public repositories).

```yaml
jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: danikdanik2013/amlint@v0.6.1
        with:
          config-path: alertmanager.yml
          sarif: true
```

- The SARIF upload runs even when the check finds problems, so code scanning shows them on
  the same run that fails.
- The job still fails on ERROR findings. To get code scanning annotations only, without the
  `github` format's annotations, also set `format: text`.
- `ignore` and `only` apply to the SARIF upload too.

## Pin the amlint version { #pinning-a-version }

By default the action installs the latest amlint from PyPI, so a new release with new
checks can start failing your build. To choose when you upgrade, set `version`:

```yaml
      - uses: danikdanik2013/amlint@v0.6.1
        with:
          config-path: alertmanager.yml
          version: '0.6.1'
```

Don't pin below `0.4.1`: the default `format: github` needs `0.4.0`, and `diff-base` needs
`0.4.1`. The formats on the [Kubernetes & Mimir](kubernetes.md) page need `0.5.0` or later, and the
**Changed routes** diagram in the PR comment needs `0.6.0`.

## Limits

- `config-path` takes one file. To lint several, add a step per file.
- There are no inputs for `--input-format`, `--matcher-strategy` or `--rules`. If you need
  them, install amlint and run it yourself:

    ```yaml
          - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
            with:
              python-version: '3.12'
          - run: pip install amlint
          - run: amlint check values.yaml --input-format helm --format github
    ```


---

Source: https://danikdanik2013.github.io/amlint/fidelity/

# Verified against Alertmanager

amlint simulates Alertmanager in Python instead of running it. This page shows how CI checks
that the simulation matches the real Alertmanager, and lists the few places where it doesn't.

[![Alertmanager differential](https://github.com/danikdanik2013/amlint/actions/workflows/differential.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/danikdanik2013/amlint/actions/workflows/differential.yml)

!!! success "The promise"
    On generated configs and alerts, amlint gives **the same receivers, the same inhibitions
    and the same rejected configs** as **Alertmanager 0.32.2, 0.33.1 and 0.34.1**.

    Each pull request that changes the simulation is checked on 300 routing configs (with
    several alerts each), 300 configs for config errors and 40 inhibition scenarios, against
    each of the three versions. A weekly run tries 1,500 + 1,500 + 150 new ones.

What this means for you:

- `amlint route`, `amlint test` and the routing part of `amlint diff` pick the receivers
  your Alertmanager would pick, in the same order.
- `amlint route --firing` and `firing:` in tests mute an alert exactly when Alertmanager
  would.
- When `amlint check` reports an error that it marks as also caught by amtool (`amlint list`
  shows a ✓), Alertmanager refuses to load the config, and the other way round.
- Where amlint can't reproduce Alertmanager exactly, such as Unicode classes in regexes
  (`\pL`), `route` and `test` exit 2 and tell you to use `amtool config routes test`. They
  never guess.
- The exceptions are listed under [Known differences](#known-differences).

## What is compared

| | amlint | Alertmanager |
|---|---|---|
| **Routing** | the receivers amlint's router returns, in order | `amtool config routes test --config.file=… label=value …` |
| **Config errors** | an error-level finding whose code `amlint list` marks ✓ (also caught by amtool) | `amtool check-config` rejects the config |
| **Inhibition** | whether amlint's inhibitor mutes each alert | `status.inhibitedBy` from `GET /api/v2/alerts` on a running `alertmanager`, after `POST /api/v2/alerts` |

The inhibition test also compares each alert's receivers from the API, which is a second,
independent routing check against the server itself.

How the job runs (`.github/workflows/differential.yml`):

- **Versions:** the last two minor releases and the newest, 0.32.2, 0.33.1 and 0.34.1. It
  downloads the official release tarballs and checks their sha256 against values pinned in
  the workflow. A weekly job warns when a newer Alertmanager release is out.
- **When:** on pull requests and pushes to `main` that change the simulation, the checks,
  how configs are read, or the tests, and weekly.
- **Cases:** [Hypothesis](https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io), a property-based testing
  library, generates the configs and alerts from a seed. Pull requests and pushes use seed
  0, so every run tests the same cases. The weekly run uses a fresh seed to find new ones.

## What the generated configs cover

- route trees up to four levels deep, with `continue: true` / `false` fan-out and inherited
  receivers
- `=`, `!=`, `=~` and `!~` matchers in every spelling Alertmanager accepts: `matchers:`
  entries with one or several matchers, with or without `{}`, quoted, loosely escaped
  (`"a\.b"`) or bare values, spaces around the operator, quoted label names
  (`"service.name"="api"`), and `match:` / `match_re:` maps
- regexes from a pool of real-world patterns and built from parts: alternations, groups,
  classes, quantifiers, `^ $ \A \z \b \B`, `(?i)`, `(?s)`, `(?m)`
- label values that stress quoting and matching: quotes, backslashes, commas, braces,
  newlines, non-ASCII letters (`é`, the Kelvin sign), and plain YAML scalars that YAML 1.1
  would type (`NO`, `1.10`, `0x1F`)
- label sets with labels missing, empty, or set to values the matchers look for
- configs with up to two of the mistakes `amtool check-config` rejects, including
  integration fields covered (or not) by a `_file` variant or a `global:` default,
  `matchers:` entries that neither matcher parser reads, and `match:` / `match_re:` keys
  that aren't classic label names (`k8s.ns`, `1a`, a null key)
- inhibit rules with `equal:`, rules matching both sides, and alerts that match several
  rules

When amlint and Alertmanager disagree, the test reduces the case to a minimal config and
label set that still disagree. It prints both results and the `amtool` command that
reproduces it. To run the tests yourself, see
[Contributing](contributing.md#differential-tests-against-alertmanager).

## Known differences

Each of these is deliberate, depends on how Alertmanager was built, or is an Alertmanager
bug. The tests recognize each one narrowly and count it in their statistics, so none is
skipped silently.

- **Inhibition before Alertmanager 0.34.1.** Older releases keep one source alert per
  inhibit rule and `equal:` value. If that alert matches both sides of the rule, they miss
  the inhibition, even when another firing alert would inhibit. So the result depends on
  the order the alerts arrived. 0.34.1 fixed this (#5449, #5542, #5559), and amlint follows
  0.34.1. If you run 0.32 or 0.33, Alertmanager may not mute an alert that amlint says is
  muted, but only when another firing alert matches both sides of the rule.
- **Regexes amlint declines.** Python can't evaluate Unicode classes (`\pL`, `\p{Greek}`) or
  negated POSIX classes (`[[:^alpha:]]`) the way Go does. For these, `amlint route` and
  `amlint test` exit 2 and point you to `amtool config routes test`. `amlint check` still
  accepts them as valid regexes.
- **Unknown Unicode class names.** `amlint check` doesn't report a `\p{...}` class Go doesn't
  know, such as `\p{Foo}`, but Alertmanager rejects it ("invalid character class range").
  Which names are valid depends on the Go version Alertmanager was built with: Go 1.25 added
  aliases such as `\p{Letter}` and made names case-insensitive. So `\p{greek}` works in
  Alertmanager 0.32 to 0.34 (built with Go 1.26), but not in builds with older Go.
- **Configs Alertmanager won't load.** `amlint route` and `amlint test` still simulate a
  config with errors that `amlint check` reports, such as an undefined receiver or a root
  route without a receiver. `amlint diff` relies on this to compare a new file against an
  empty config. The config-error test covers these errors through `amlint check`.

## Alertmanager behavior amlint matches { #differences-it-found-now-fixed }

The differential tests found these surprising Alertmanager behaviors. amlint now behaves the
same way, and `amlint check` reports the cases that are probably not what you meant.

- **YAML scalars.** Alertmanager reads `match: {country: NO}` as the string `NO`, although
  YAML 1.1 says `false`. `1.10`, `0x1F`, `yes` and the like keep their text too, in a plain
  config and in one held in a Secret or a Mimir config. Helm values are different: Helm
  reads `values.yaml` as YAML 1.1 before it renders the config, so there `NO` really is
  `false`, and amlint reads it that way.
- **Bare regexes with braces.** Alertmanager strips one trailing `}` from a `matchers:` entry
  even when the entry doesn't start with `{`. So a bare `code=~[0-9]{3}` is the regex
  `[0-9]{3`, which matches `1{3` and not `123`. Quote the value (`code=~"[0-9]{3}"`) to get
  what you meant. `amlint check` warns about it (`stripped-brace`).
- **Which matcher parser reads an entry.** Alertmanager has two matcher parsers: the classic
  one and a newer UTF-8 one. The classic parser reads an entry whenever it can, even where
  the UTF-8 one would read it differently. Only when it fails, for example on a quoted label
  name, does the UTF-8 parser read the whole entry, with Go string escapes: there `\t` is a
  tab and `\.` is an error. Bare values are unescaped like quoted ones (`a=x\\y` is `x\y`).
  `amlint check` reports an entry neither parser reads as `bad-matcher`.
- **Regex details.** `\b` and `\B` look at ASCII word characters only and ignore `(?i)`, and
  `\B` matches an empty value. `$` outside `(?m)` doesn't match before a final newline. A
  quantifier after an anchor (`^*`, `\b+`) is valid in Go; `[\b]` is not.
- **Config errors.** `group_by: ['...', alertname]` is an error, since Alertmanager refuses
  it. An empty `api_url: ""` in `slack_configs` is an error, even with
  `global.slack_api_url` set. `match:` keys that aren't classic label names (`k8s.ns`) are
  rejected (`bad-match-label`); use a quoted name in `matchers:` for those.

## Not covered yet

- Alerts use label names from a small pool.
- `group_by`, timings and time intervals aren't compared, because amtool doesn't print them.
  The inhibition test reads only receivers and inhibitions from the API.
- Only `matchers:` entries, `match:` maps, receivers and inhibit rules are generated.
  Integration settings beyond the fields amlint checks, templates, and YAML features such as
  anchors and merge keys are not.


---

Source: https://danikdanik2013.github.io/amlint/checks/

# Checks overview

amlint's checks catch Alertmanager config mistakes that lose alerts, send them to the wrong
place, or mute them when they shouldn't be.

amlint has **38 checks**. `amtool check-config` also catches **20** of them: Alertmanager
refuses to load those configs, and amlint reports them so one run covers everything. The
other **18** are configs that amtool accepts and Alertmanager runs, just not the way you
meant. Those are the main reason to run amlint.

The three **Prometheus rules** checks run only with `amlint check --rules`, which compares
your routes and inhibition rules with the alerts your Prometheus rule files define. See
[Prometheus rules](rules.md).

From the CLI, [`amlint list`](../usage.md#list) prints the same list, and
[`amlint explain <code>`](../usage.md#explain) explains one check.

## All checks

Grouped by page, then by level. ✓ in the **amtool** column means `amtool check-config`
catches it too.

| area | check | level | amtool | what it flags |
|------|-------|-------|:------:|---------------|
| Routing | [`no-root-route`](routing.md#no-root-route) | error | ✓ | The config has no `route:` key. |
| Routing | [`invalid-root-route`](routing.md#invalid-root-route) | error | ✓ | The root route has no receiver, or has matchers, `continue: true` or time intervals. |
| Routing | [`undefined-receiver`](routing.md#undefined-receiver) | error | ✓ | A route names a receiver that isn't defined in `receivers:`. |
| Routing | [`groupby-ellipsis`](routing.md#groupby-ellipsis) | error | ✓ | `group_by` lists `'...'` next to label names. |
| Routing | [`bad-regex`](routing.md#bad-regex) | error | ✓ | A regex doesn't compile, or uses syntax Go RE2 doesn't support, like lookahead. |
| Routing | [`bad-matcher`](routing.md#bad-matcher) | error | ✓ | A `matchers:` entry Alertmanager can't parse. |
| Routing | [`bad-match-label`](routing.md#bad-match-label) | error | ✓ | A `match:` or `match_re:` key that isn't a classic label name, like `k8s.ns`. |
| Routing | [`unreachable-route`](routing.md#unreachable-route) | warn | | A catch-all route without `continue: true` hides the sibling routes after it. |
| Routing | [`route-match-collision`](routing.md#route-match-collision) | warn | | Two sibling routes have identical matchers; the second never gets alerts. |
| Routing | [`shadowed-route`](routing.md#shadowed-route) | warn | | An earlier sibling route matches every alert this route matches; this one never gets alerts. |
| Routing | [`stripped-brace`](routing.md#stripped-brace) | warn | | A bare matcher value ends in `}`, which Alertmanager strips off. |
| Routing | [`useless-continue`](routing.md#useless-continue) | info | | `continue: true` on the last sibling route does nothing. |
| Routing | [`deep-nesting`](routing.md#deep-nesting) | info | | The routing tree is more than 5 levels deep. |
| Receivers | [`duplicate-receiver`](receivers.md#duplicate-receiver) | error | ✓ | Two receivers share the same name. |
| Receivers | [`email-no-smarthost`](receivers.md#email-no-smarthost) | error | ✓ | An `email_configs` entry has no `smarthost`, and `global.smtp_smarthost` isn't set. |
| Receivers | [`webhook-no-url`](receivers.md#webhook-no-url) | error | ✓ | A `webhook_configs` entry has no `url` or `url_file`. |
| Receivers | [`pagerduty-no-routing-key`](receivers.md#pagerduty-no-routing-key) | error | ✓ | A `pagerduty_configs` entry has no `routing_key` or `service_key` (or their `_file` forms). |
| Receivers | [`slack-no-api-url`](receivers.md#slack-no-api-url) | error | ✓ | A `slack_configs` entry has no `api_url`, and `global.slack_api_url` isn't set. |
| Receivers | [`opsgenie-no-api-key`](receivers.md#opsgenie-no-api-key) | error | ✓ | An `opsgenie_configs` entry has no `api_key`, and `global.opsgenie_api_key` isn't set. |
| Receivers | [`msteams-no-webhook-url`](receivers.md#msteams-no-webhook-url) | error | ✓ | An `msteams_configs` entry has no `webhook_url` or `webhook_url_file`. |
| Receivers | [`telegram-no-bot-token`](receivers.md#telegram-no-bot-token) | error | ✓ | A `telegram_configs` entry has no `bot_token` or `bot_token_file`. |
| Receivers | [`discord-no-webhook-url`](receivers.md#discord-no-webhook-url) | error | ✓ | A `discord_configs` entry has no `webhook_url` or `webhook_url_file`. |
| Receivers | [`victorops-no-api-key`](receivers.md#victorops-no-api-key) | error | ✓ | A `victorops_configs` entry has no `api_key`, and `global.victorops_api_key` isn't set. |
| Receivers | [`wechat-no-corp-id`](receivers.md#wechat-no-corp-id) | error | ✓ | A `wechat_configs` entry has no `corp_id`, and `global.wechat_api_corp_id` isn't set. |
| Receivers | [`sns-no-target`](receivers.md#sns-no-target) | error | ✓ | An `sns_configs` entry has none of `topic_arn`, `phone_number` or `target_arn`. |
| Receivers | [`template-file-missing`](receivers.md#template-file-missing) | error | | A relative `templates:` path matches no file next to the config (warn for a glob). |
| Receivers | [`empty-receiver`](receivers.md#empty-receiver) | warn | | A receiver has no integration, like `slack_configs` (info for the root route's receiver or one named like `null`). |
| Receivers | [`unused-receiver`](receivers.md#unused-receiver) | info | | A receiver no route uses. |
| Inhibition | [`inhibit-no-equal`](inhibition.md#inhibit-no-equal) | warn | | An inhibition rule has no `equal:` field. |
| Inhibition | [`circular-inhibition`](inhibition.md#circular-inhibition) | warn | | Two inhibition rules can mute each other. |
| Inhibition | [`inhibit-same-match`](inhibition.md#inhibit-same-match) | info | | The source and target side of an inhibition rule share a `label="value"`. |
| Timing | [`undefined-time-interval`](timing.md#undefined-time-interval) | error | ✓ | `mute_time_intervals` or `active_time_intervals` names an interval that isn't defined. |
| Timing | [`repeat-before-group`](timing.md#repeat-before-group) | warn | | `repeat_interval` is shorter than `group_interval`. |
| Timing | [`wait-exceeds-interval`](timing.md#wait-exceeds-interval) | warn | | `group_wait` is longer than `group_interval`. |
| Timing | [`global-resolve-timeout-missing`](timing.md#global-resolve-timeout-missing) | info | | `global.resolve_timeout` isn't set, so Alertmanager uses its default of `5m`. |
| Prometheus rules | [`route-unknown-alertname`](rules.md#route-unknown-alertname) | warn | | With `--rules`: a route matches an `alertname` no alerting rule produces. |
| Prometheus rules | [`inhibit-unknown-alertname`](rules.md#inhibit-unknown-alertname) | warn | | With `--rules`: an inhibition rule's source or target matches an `alertname` no alerting rule produces. |
| Prometheus rules | [`alert-hits-default-receiver`](rules.md#alert-hits-default-receiver) | info | | With `--rules`: alerts match no child route, by their static labels, and go to the root route's receiver. |

## Severity levels

| level | meaning |
|-------|---------|
| **error** | Alertmanager refuses the config, or notifications can't be delivered as configured. |
| **warn** | The config loads, but almost certainly doesn't do what you meant. |
| **info** | Worth a look. Often intentional. |

`amlint check` exits `1` on an error finding. Warnings fail it only with `--strict`. See
[exit codes](../usage.md#exit-codes).

## Ignoring checks

**For a whole repo:** list checks to skip, or change a check's level, in `.amlint.yml` in
the directory you run amlint from (`[tool.amlint]` in `pyproject.toml` works too). See
[project config](../usage.md#project-config).

```yaml title=".amlint.yml"
ignore:
  - unused-receiver
severity:
  empty-receiver: info       # warn → info
  deep-nesting: warn         # info → warn
```

**For one run:** `amlint check alertmanager.yml --ignore deep-nesting,unused-receiver`, or
`--only bad-regex` to show nothing else.

**For one spot in the config:** add a comment, so the exception and its reason sit next to
the config. See [inline suppressions](../usage.md#inline-suppressions).

```yaml
# amlint: disable-file=global-resolve-timeout-missing

route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - receiver: catch-all   # amlint: disable=unreachable-route
    - matchers: [team="infra"]
      receiver: infra
```

- `# amlint: disable=<code>,<code>` at the end of a line silences those checks on that line.
- The same comment on a line of its own silences them on the next line of YAML.
- `# amlint: disable-file=<code>,<code>` in the comment block at the top of the file, before
  any YAML, silences them for the whole file.

A finding's line is the one amlint prints with it.


---

Source: https://danikdanik2013.github.io/amlint/checks/routing/

# Routing checks

These checks catch two kinds of routing mistakes: a routing tree Alertmanager refuses to
load, and routes that load fine but never get the alerts you meant for them.

A **route** is a node in the `route:` tree. Its **matchers** (label conditions such as
`severity="critical"`, written under `matchers:`, `match:` or `match_re:`) pick alerts, and
its **receiver** (a named entry under `receivers:`) gets them. Routes in the same `routes:`
list are **siblings**: Alertmanager tries them top to bottom and stops at the first match,
unless that route sets **`continue: true`** ("keep trying the siblings below me").

To see where a given alert ends up, run
[`amlint route alertmanager.yml team=infra severity=critical`](../usage.md#route).

---

## no-root-route

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** The config has no `route:` key, so there is no routing tree.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: default
    webhook_configs:
      - url: http://alerts.example.com/hook
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config: `no routes provided`.

**How to fix:** Add a root route that names the receiver every alert falls back to.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
receivers:
  - name: default
    webhook_configs:
      - url: http://alerts.example.com/hook
```

---

## invalid-root-route

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** The root route (the top-level `route:`, which every alert enters)
breaks one of Alertmanager's rules for it. It must name a `receiver`, and it can't have
matchers, `continue: true`, `mute_time_intervals` or `active_time_intervals`.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  matchers: [team="infra"]   # the root route must match every alert
  routes:                    # ...and it has no receiver
    - matchers: [severity="critical"]
      receiver: pager
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config, with an error such as
`root route must specify a default receiver` or `root route must not have any matchers`.
amlint reports every broken rule at once.

**How to fix:** Give the root route a receiver. Move matchers and time intervals down to a
child route.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default          # gets every alert no child route matches
  routes:
    - matchers: [team="infra", severity="critical"]
      receiver: pager
```

---

## undefined-receiver

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A route names a receiver that isn't defined under `receivers:`.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [team="infra"]
      receiver: pager-team   # not defined below
receivers:
  - name: default
    webhook_configs:
      - url: http://alerts.example.com/hook
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config:
`undefined receiver "pager-team" used in route`.

**How to fix:** Define the receiver, or correct the name to one that exists.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [team="infra"]
      receiver: pager-team
receivers:
  - name: default
    webhook_configs:
      - url: http://alerts.example.com/hook
  - name: pager-team         # added
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: <integration-key>
```

---

## groupby-ellipsis

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A route's `group_by` (the labels that decide which alerts share one
notification) lists `'...'` next to label names. `'...'` already means "group by every
label".

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  group_by: ['...', alertname, cluster]
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config:
``cannot have wildcard group_by (`...`) and other labels at the same time``.

**How to fix:** Keep either `'...'` or the label names, not both.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  group_by: [alertname, cluster]   # or: ['...']
```

---

## bad-regex

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A regex matcher (`=~` or `!~`) doesn't compile, or uses syntax that
Go's RE2 engine, which Alertmanager uses, doesn't have: lookahead or lookbehind,
backreferences, possessive quantifiers, atomic groups, or a repeat count over 1000. amlint
checks regexes in routes and in inhibition rules.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - service=~"(?!test-).*"   # lookahead: RE2 has none
      receiver: team
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the whole config
(`error parsing regexp: invalid or unsupported Perl syntax`), so no route works, not just
this one.

**How to fix:** Rewrite the regex in RE2 syntax. To exclude values, use a negative matcher
(`!~`) instead of a lookahead.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - service!~"test-.*"       # every service not starting with test-
      receiver: team
```

---

## bad-matcher

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** An entry under `matchers:` (or `source_matchers:` / `target_matchers:`
in an inhibition rule) is not a matcher Alertmanager can parse. Common causes:

- an empty matcher between two commas: `a=b,,c=d`
- a stray double quote: `a=b"c`
- a comma in a bare (unquoted) value, which splits the entry: `a=b, c=~x{1,2}`
- a quoted label name, such as `"service.name"=...`, followed by a value that isn't a valid
  Go string: `"x.y"="a\.b"` (`\.` is not a Go escape), or a bare value with a backslash or
  brace (`"x.y"=~\d+`)

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - 'service=api,,env=prod'        # empty matcher between the commas
        - '"service.name"=~"api\.v2"'   # \. is not a Go escape
      receiver: team
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config (`bad matcher format: ...` or
`matcher value contains unescaped double quote: ...`). It reads each entry with its classic
parser, and with its UTF-8 parser only if the classic one fails. amlint flags the entries
both parsers reject.

**How to fix:** Write each matcher as `label="value"` (or `!=`, `=~`, `!~`), with one comma
between matchers. A quoted label name sends the whole entry to the UTF-8 parser, where
values are Go strings: quote the value and double each backslash.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - 'service="api", env="prod"'
        - '"service.name"=~"api\\.v2"'  # \\ is one backslash in a Go string
      receiver: team
```

---

## bad-match-label

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A key under `match:` or `match_re:` isn't a classic label name: a
letter or underscore, then letters, digits and underscores (`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`).
Inhibition rules' `source_match`, `target_match` and their `_re` forms are checked too.
Names like `k8s.namespace` only work in `matchers:`, quoted.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - match:
        k8s.namespace: payments   # not a classic label name
      receiver: payments
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config:
`invalid label name "k8s.namespace"`.

**How to fix:** Move the matcher to `matchers:` (or `source_matchers:` /
`target_matchers:`) and quote the label name. For a child route or an inhibition rule, the
amlint finding spells out the entry to use.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - '"k8s.namespace"="payments"'   # quoted: any UTF-8 name works
      receiver: payments
```

---

## unreachable-route

**Level:** warn · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** A catch-all route (no matchers, or only `label=~".*"` matchers) without
`continue: true` sits above other siblings. It takes every alert, so the siblings below it
never get any.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - receiver: team-slack       # no matchers: matches every alert
    - matchers: [severity="critical"]
      receiver: pager            # never reached
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Loads the config. Every alert goes to `team-slack` and stops
there, so `pager` never gets an alert.

**How to fix:** Put the catch-all last. If every alert should reach the catch-all *and* the
routes below it, give it `continue: true`.

=== "Catch-all last"

    ```yaml title="Fixed"
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [severity="critical"]
          receiver: pager
        - receiver: team-slack
    ```

=== "Notify both"

    ```yaml title="Fixed"
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - receiver: team-slack
          continue: true         # keep trying the routes below
        - matchers: [severity="critical"]
          receiver: pager
    ```

---

## route-match-collision

**Level:** warn · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** Two sibling routes have identical matchers, and the first one has no
`continue: true`. Different spellings of the same matcher count as identical:
`match: {team: infra}` and `matchers: [team="infra"]`.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [team="infra", severity="critical"]
      receiver: pager
    - matchers: [team="infra", severity="critical"]   # same matchers
      receiver: infra-slack                            # never reached
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Loads the config. Every matching alert stops at the first
route, so `infra-slack` never gets an alert.

**How to fix:** If both receivers should get these alerts, add `continue: true` to the
first route. Otherwise, give the second route different matchers, or remove it.

=== "Notify both"

    ```yaml title="Fixed"
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [team="infra", severity="critical"]
          receiver: pager
          continue: true         # keep trying the routes below
        - matchers: [team="infra", severity="critical"]
          receiver: infra-slack
    ```

=== "Different matchers"

    ```yaml title="Fixed"
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [team="infra", severity="critical"]
          receiver: pager
        - matchers: [team="infra", severity="warning"]
          receiver: infra-slack
    ```

---

## shadowed-route

**Level:** warn · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** An earlier sibling without `continue: true` matches every alert this
route matches, even though their matchers differ. amlint compares the label values each
matcher allows, not how it's written. In each pair below, the earlier route hides the later
one:

- `severity=~"warning|critical"` before `severity="critical"`: `critical` matches the regex
- `team!="db"` before `team="infra"`: `infra` is not `db`
- `alertname=~"Kube.*"` before `alertname=~"KubePod.*"`: every `KubePod…` name starts with
  `Kube`
- `service!~"db-.*"` before `service=~"api-[0-9]+"`: no `api-…` name starts with `db-`
- `team=~"|infra"` before `team=""`: a missing label counts as the empty string, as in
  Alertmanager
- `severity="critical"` before `severity="critical", team="infra"`: the earlier route asks
  for less

Parent routes count too, because every alert that reaches the siblings matched their
parents. Under a parent with `env="prod"`, a sibling with
`env=~"prod|staging", severity="critical"` hides a later sibling with `severity="critical"`.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [severity=~"warning|critical"]
      receiver: ops
    - matchers: [severity="critical"]   # never reached
      receiver: pager
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Loads the config. Critical alerts match the first route and
stop there, so `pager` never gets them.

**How to fix:** Put the narrower route first. If both receivers should get the alerts, give
the broader route `continue: true` instead.

=== "Narrower first"

    ```yaml title="Fixed"
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [severity="critical"]
          receiver: pager
        - matchers: [severity=~"warning|critical"]
          receiver: ops
    ```

=== "Notify both"

    ```yaml title="Fixed"
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [severity=~"warning|critical"]
          receiver: ops
          continue: true         # keep trying the routes below
        - matchers: [severity="critical"]
          receiver: pager
    ```

**Limits:** amlint reports only routes it can prove dead. It stays silent when a regex uses
case folding (`(?i)`), word boundaries (`\b`), anchors anywhere but the very start or end,
or is too large to compare, even if the route is in fact dead. Each dead route gets one
finding: identical matchers are [`route-match-collision`](#route-match-collision), and a
catch-all sibling is [`unreachable-route`](#unreachable-route).

---

## stripped-brace

**Level:** warn · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** A bare (unquoted) value at the end of a `matchers:` entry ends in `}`,
and the entry doesn't start with `{`. Alertmanager drops that `}`. Entries in routes and in
inhibition rules' `source_matchers` / `target_matchers` are checked.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - code=~[0-9]{3}      # Alertmanager reads the regex as [0-9]{3
      receiver: http-errors
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Loads the config. Its classic matcher parser strips one trailing
`}` from every entry, braces or not. The regex here becomes `[0-9]{3`, which matches the
text `1{3` and not `123`, so the route never matches the alerts you meant.

**How to fix:** Quote the value, or wrap the whole entry in braces.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - code=~"[0-9]{3}"    # or: '{code=~[0-9]{3}}'
      receiver: http-errors
```

---

## useless-continue

**Level:** info · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** The last route in a `routes:` list has `continue: true`. No sibling
comes after it, so the flag does nothing.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [env="prod"]
      receiver: team
      continue: true           # last sibling: nothing to continue to
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Ignores the flag. `continue` only passes the alert on to later
siblings in the same `routes:` list, never to the routes after the parent.

**How to fix:** Remove `continue: true`. If you meant alerts to also reach the routes after
the parent, set `continue: true` on the parent instead.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [env="prod"]
      receiver: team
```

---

## deep-nesting

**Level:** info · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** The routing tree goes more than 5 levels below the root route. That
is hard to read, review and debug.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [env="prod"]
      routes:
        - matchers: [region="eu"]
          routes:
            - matchers: [team="infra"]
              routes:
                - matchers: [service="db"]
                  routes:
                    - matchers: [severity="critical"]
                      routes:
                        - matchers: [component="disk"]   # level 6
                          receiver: db-pager
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Routes alerts as usual. It has no depth limit.

**How to fix:** Flatten the tree. One route with several matchers replaces a chain of
single-matcher routes.

```yaml title="Fixed"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers:
        - env="prod"
        - region="eu"
        - team="infra"
        - service="db"
        - severity="critical"
        - component="disk"
      receiver: db-pager
```


---

Source: https://danikdanik2013.github.io/amlint/checks/receivers/

# Receiver checks

A **receiver** is a named destination for alerts: routes (the branches of the `route:` tree
that pick alerts by their labels) send each alert to one. Each receiver holds one or more
**integrations**, such as `slack_configs`, `pagerduty_configs`, `email_configs` or
`webhook_configs`, which do the actual sending. These checks catch receivers that can't
deliver (a duplicate name, no integration, a missing URL, key or template file) and
receivers that no route uses.

**amtool** below is `amtool check-config`, Alertmanager's own config checker. "Also catches
it" means Alertmanager refuses the config anyway. "Doesn't catch it" means Alertmanager
loads and runs the config without complaint, so only amlint tells you.

---

## duplicate-receiver

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** Two receivers have the same `name`.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    webhook_configs:
      - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/team'
  - name: team                  # same name again
    webhook_configs:
      - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/oncall'
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Refuses to load the config (`notification config name "team"
is not unique`). It doesn't use one and ignore the other. amlint points at the second
definition.

**How to fix:** Rename one of them, or merge them, because one receiver can hold several
integrations.

=== "Rename"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: team
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/team'
      - name: team-oncall         # point the route that needs it here
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/oncall'
    ```

=== "Merge"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: team
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/team'
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/oncall'
    ```

---

## empty-receiver

**Level:** warn, or info when the drop looks intentional · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** A receiver has no integration, so alerts routed to it go nowhere. An
empty list such as `webhook_configs: []` also counts as no integration.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
  routes:
    - matchers: [severity="critical"]
      receiver: pager
receivers:
  - name: default
    webhook_configs:
      - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/default'
  - name: pager                 # no integration
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Loads the config and routes critical alerts to `pager`. Then it
silently drops them.

**How to fix:** Add an integration. If you mean to drop the alerts, make that clear: make
it the default receiver (the `receiver:` at the top of `route:`), or name it `null`,
`blackhole`, `devnull`, `dev-null`, `discard` or `drop` (in any case). amlint then reports
it as info, not warn.

=== "Fixed"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: default
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/default'
      - name: pager
        pagerduty_configs:
          - routing_key: 'your-pagerduty-integration-key'
    ```

=== "Intentional drop"
    ```yaml
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [alertname="Watchdog"]
          receiver: 'null'
    receivers:
      - name: default
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/default'
      - name: 'null'              # drops Watchdog on purpose: info, not warn
    ```

Quote `'null'`. Unquoted, YAML reads `null` as no value, not as the name `null`.

**Limits:** amlint knows these integrations: `email`, `pagerduty`, `slack`, `opsgenie`,
`victorops`, `webhook`, `wechat`, `sns`, `msteams`, `msteamsv2`, `telegram`, `discord`,
`pushover`, `webex`, `jira`, `rocketchat`, `incidentio` and `mattermost` (each as
`<name>_configs`). It
reports a receiver that uses only some other key as empty.

---

## unused-receiver

**Level:** info · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** A receiver is defined, but no route sends alerts to it. Usually it's
left over from an older config.

```yaml title="Bad"
route:
  receiver: default
receivers:
  - name: default
    webhook_configs:
      - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/default'
  - name: old-pager             # no route uses it
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: 'your-pagerduty-integration-key'
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Loads it and never sends anything to it. That's harmless, but
it's clutter, and readers may think alerts go there.

**How to fix:** Delete the receiver, or add a route that uses it.

=== "Delete it"
    ```yaml
    route:
      receiver: default
    receivers:
      - name: default
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/default'
    ```

=== "Route to it"
    ```yaml
    route:
      receiver: default
      routes:
        - matchers: [severity="critical"]
          receiver: old-pager
    receivers:
      - name: default
        webhook_configs:
          - url: 'http://hooks.example.com/default'
      - name: old-pager
        pagerduty_configs:
          - routing_key: 'your-pagerduty-integration-key'
    ```

---

## template-file-missing

**Level:** error for a file path, warn for a glob · **amtool:** doesn't catch it

**What goes wrong:** A relative path under `templates:` matches no file. These files hold
the notification templates (`{{ define "..." }}`) that your integrations use.

```yaml title="Bad"
templates:
  - templates/custom.tmpl       # no such file next to alertmanager.yml: error
  - tmpl/*.tmpl                 # glob that matches no file: warn
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Resolves relative paths against the config file's directory.
It starts even when a path matches nothing, but it loads no templates from that path, so
notifications that use those templates fail to render.

**How to fix:** Correct the path, or add the file. Paths are relative to the config file.

```yaml title="Fixed"
templates:
  - templates/custom.tmpl       # exists next to alertmanager.yml
  - templates/*.tmpl            # matches at least one file
```

**Limits:**

- amlint doesn't check absolute paths (`/etc/alertmanager/templates/*.tmpl`). They point
  into the Alertmanager host or container, not to where amlint runs.
- amlint doesn't run this check on a plain config read from stdin (`amlint check -`),
  because there's no directory to resolve the paths against.
- For a Kubernetes Secret or kube-prometheus-stack values, amlint checks entries against
  the template files that ship with the config, not against files on disk. See
  [Kubernetes & Mimir](../kubernetes.md#kubernetes-secrets).

---

## Missing integration fields

Each integration needs one field before it can send anything: a server, a URL, a key or a
target. If that field is missing, Alertmanager rejects the whole config. It won't start,
and a reload fails and keeps the old config. All of these checks are **error** level, and
amtool also catches them. amlint includes them so that one run reports every problem, as
text, JSON or SARIF, without the Go binary.

| check | integration | needs | or instead |
|-------|-------------|-------|------------|
| [`email-no-smarthost`](#email-no-smarthost) | `email_configs` | `smarthost` | `global.smtp_smarthost` |
| [`webhook-no-url`](#webhook-no-url) | `webhook_configs` | `url` | `url_file` |
| [`pagerduty-no-routing-key`](#pagerduty-no-routing-key) | `pagerduty_configs` | `routing_key` | `routing_key_file`, `service_key`, `service_key_file` |
| [`slack-no-api-url`](#slack-no-api-url) | `slack_configs` | `api_url` | `api_url_file`, `global.slack_api_url`, `global.slack_api_url_file` |
| [`opsgenie-no-api-key`](#opsgenie-no-api-key) | `opsgenie_configs` | `api_key` | `api_key_file`, `global.opsgenie_api_key`, `global.opsgenie_api_key_file` |
| [`msteams-no-webhook-url`](#msteams-no-webhook-url) | `msteams_configs` | `webhook_url` | `webhook_url_file` |
| [`telegram-no-bot-token`](#telegram-no-bot-token) | `telegram_configs` | `bot_token` | `bot_token_file` |
| [`discord-no-webhook-url`](#discord-no-webhook-url) | `discord_configs` | `webhook_url` | `webhook_url_file` |
| [`victorops-no-api-key`](#victorops-no-api-key) | `victorops_configs` | `api_key` | `api_key_file`, `global.victorops_api_key`, `global.victorops_api_key_file` |
| [`wechat-no-corp-id`](#wechat-no-corp-id) | `wechat_configs` | `corp_id` | `global.wechat_api_corp_id` |
| [`sns-no-target`](#sns-no-target) | `sns_configs` | one of `topic_arn`, `phone_number`, `target_arn` | none |

- A `*_file` field reads the value from a file, which keeps the secret out of the config.
- A `global.*` field is the default for every entry of that integration that doesn't set
  its own.
- A field set to an empty string (`url: ''`) counts as missing.

---

## email-no-smarthost

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** An `email_configs` entry has no `smarthost` (the SMTP server, as
`host:port`), and `global.smtp_smarthost` isn't set.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    email_configs:
      - to: 'team@example.com'
        from: 'alertmanager@example.com'
        # no smarthost
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

**How to fix:** Set `smarthost` on the entry, or set `global.smtp_smarthost` once for all
email entries.

=== "On the entry"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: team
        email_configs:
          - to: 'team@example.com'
            from: 'alertmanager@example.com'
            smarthost: 'smtp.example.com:587'
    ```

=== "Global default"
    ```yaml
    global:
      smtp_smarthost: 'smtp.example.com:587'
      smtp_from: 'alertmanager@example.com'
    receivers:
      - name: team
        email_configs:
          - to: 'team@example.com'
    ```

---

## webhook-no-url

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A `webhook_configs` entry has no `url` and no `url_file`.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    webhook_configs:
      - send_resolved: true     # no url
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

**How to fix:** Set `url`, or set `url_file` to read the URL from a file.

```yaml title="Fixed"
receivers:
  - name: team
    webhook_configs:
      - url: 'http://my-service/webhook'
        send_resolved: true
```

---

## pagerduty-no-routing-key

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A `pagerduty_configs` entry has no PagerDuty integration key. None of
`routing_key`, `routing_key_file`, `service_key` or `service_key_file` is set.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: pager
    pagerduty_configs:
      - severity: critical      # no routing_key
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

**How to fix:** Set `routing_key`, or `routing_key_file` to read it from a file. amlint
also accepts `service_key` and `service_key_file`.

```yaml title="Fixed"
receivers:
  - name: pager
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: 'your-pagerduty-integration-key'
        severity: critical
```

---

## slack-no-api-url

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A `slack_configs` entry has no Slack webhook URL. It has no `api_url`
or `api_url_file`, and neither `global.slack_api_url` nor `global.slack_api_url_file` is
set. amlint also flags an empty `api_url: ''`, even when a global URL is set.

=== "Bad: no URL"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: team
        slack_configs:
          - channel: '#alerts'    # no api_url, and no global one
    ```

=== "Bad: empty api_url"
    ```yaml
    global:
      slack_api_url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX'
    receivers:
      - name: team
        slack_configs:
          - channel: '#alerts'
            api_url: ''           # empty: the global URL isn't used
    ```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config. An empty `api_url` doesn't fall back to
the global URL. Alertmanager tries to read the empty string as a URL, and that fails.

**How to fix:** Set `api_url` (or `api_url_file`) on the entry, or set
`global.slack_api_url` (or `global.slack_api_url_file`) once for all Slack entries. Delete
any empty `api_url:` line.

=== "On the entry"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: team
        slack_configs:
          - api_url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX'
            channel: '#alerts'
    ```

=== "Global default"
    ```yaml
    global:
      slack_api_url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/T000/B000/XXXX'
    receivers:
      - name: team
        slack_configs:
          - channel: '#alerts'
    ```

---

## opsgenie-no-api-key

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** An `opsgenie_configs` entry has no `api_key` or `api_key_file`, and
neither `global.opsgenie_api_key` nor `global.opsgenie_api_key_file` is set.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    opsgenie_configs:
      - priority: P1            # no api_key
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

**How to fix:** Set `api_key` (or `api_key_file`) on the entry, or set
`global.opsgenie_api_key` (or `global.opsgenie_api_key_file`) once for all OpsGenie
entries.

=== "On the entry"
    ```yaml
    receivers:
      - name: team
        opsgenie_configs:
          - api_key: 'your-opsgenie-api-key'
            priority: P1
    ```

=== "Global default"
    ```yaml

      opsgenie_api_key: 'your-opsgenie-api-key'
    receivers:
      - name: team
        opsgenie_configs:
          - priority: P1
    ```

## msteams-no-webhook-url

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** An `msteams_configs` entry has no `webhook_url` and no
`webhook_url_file`.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    msteams_configs:
      - title: 'Alert'          # no webhook_url
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

**How to fix:** Set `webhook_url` to the Teams incoming webhook URL, or set
`webhook_url_file` to read it from a file.

```yaml title="Fixed"
receivers:
  - name: team

      - webhook_url: 'https://outlook.office.com/webhook/...'
        title: 'Alert'
```

## telegram-no-bot-token

`bot_token_file`.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    telegram_configs:
      - chat_id: -1001234567890   # no bot_token
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

```yaml title="Fixed"
receivers:
  - name: team

      - bot_token: '123456:ABC-DEF...'
        chat_id: -1001234567890
```

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
```

**What goes wrong:** A `victorops_configs` entry has no `api_key` or `api_key_file`, and

## wechat-no-corp-id

**Level:** error · **amtool:** also catches it

**What goes wrong:** A `wechat_configs` entry has no `corp_id` (your WeChat Work

this field.

```yaml title="Bad"
receivers:
  - name: team
    wechat_configs:
      - agent_id: '1000002'     # no corp_id
        api_secret: 'your-api-secret'
```

**What Alertmanager does:** Rejects the config.

**How to fix:** Set `corp_id` on the entry, or set `global.wechat_api_corp_id` once for all
WeChat entries.

=== "On the entry"
    ```yaml
    receivers:

        wechat_configs:

            agent_id: '1000002'
            api_secret: 'your-api-secret'
    ```

    ```yaml
      wechat_api_corp_id: 'your-corp-id'
    receivers:

        wechat_configs:
    ```
